summary: Potlatch Timber Protective Association lookout: 1915 platform, 1933 74-ft pole tower; destroyed 1956 or 1966 per sources that disagree.

facts.status_note: Tower destroyed; sources give 1956 or 1966. Kamstra's undated remark says the 1923 log cabin was still there.

events.note: Lookout platform about 80 ft above ground; about an acre and a half cleared of timber to widen the view (1915 annual report, as quoted by Kemnow)

Ben Thomas named as the only known staffer (Idaho Fire Lookouts). A 1919 Clearwater Republican item quoted by Kemnow puts Ben Thomas in charge of Gold Hill Lookout and the page flags the location as possibly wrong.
Log cabin. Kamstra's page says it was still there, with no date for the remark.
74 ft pole tower with 7x7 ft cab. Sources do not say it replaced the 1915 platform.

corrections.proposed: 1956 destroyed per Idaho Fire Lookouts; 1966 destroyed per firelookout.com; sources disagree
corrections.why: The idaho_fl page gives 1956 for the destruction. The 1966 date comes from firelookout.com, so the record credits the wrong source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says 1966 and Idaho Fire Lookouts says 1956. Both are cited and the story reports the disagreement without picking one.
Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Ben Thomas for 1919 at this site. Kemnow's quote of a 1919 newspaper names Gold Hill Lookout and flags the location as possibly wrong. Kept as uncertain.

sources.title: Gold Butte - Forest Lookouts
sources.publisher: Ron Kemnow, Forest Lookouts western US

notes_for_editor: Destruction year disagrees (1956 Idaho Fire Lookouts, 1966 firelookout.com); the 1966 record date is credited to idaho_fl but that page says 1956. The 1919 Ben Thomas staffing is doubtful: the quoted newspaper names Gold Hill Lookout and Kemnow flags the location as possibly wrong. height_m 22.6 is converted from the 1933 74-ft tower. Kemnow's header gives legal description 40N-3E-35, but the 1915 report quote says Sec. 36. Potlatch TPA annual reports were not opened directly; the 1915 quotes are as printed on Kemnow's page. No source describes the site today or gives access.
